tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search published ToolWiki documents. Empty query browses. Language/input/mode/finding filters apply to tool metadata only; use kind=guide for workflow instructions. Results include document IDs and section IDs.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read a ToolWiki document or section with sources, evidence scope and revision. Follow nextOffset until null to obtain all content; chunks may split code blocks. Read prerequisites and limitations before executing examples.

tools.name: compare_tools
tools.description: Compare 2-4 distinct tool profiles using the same metadata as the website. Returns requirements, scope, costs, limitations and citations.

tools.name: recommend_checks
tools.description: Evaluate a version-1 system-builder profile with the website rules. Returns candidate/details/blocked matches, missing information and gaps. Paginate with nextOffset. The profile format is documented in guides/agents-reference.

scope","url":"https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html"}],"totalChars":7788,"offset":0,"nextOffset":null,"markdown":"# Check Python linting and types together [Ruff](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/ruff/) and [mypy](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/mypy/) answer different questions. This recipe gives both the same fixture: an unused import and a call that passes text to an integer parameter. Ruff checks only `F401`; mypy checks the annotated call. Neither runs the target program. Start with [Get the examples](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/get-examples/) to download or clone the repository. From the downloaded repository's root, enter the fixture directory: ```powershell Set-Location examples/python-checks ``` [`examples/python-checks`](https://github.com/zwadhams/ToolWiki/tree/main/examples/python-checks) contains `bad/greeting.py`, the corrected `good/greeting.py`, a shared `pyproject.toml`, pinned requirements, and `run_checks.py`. **Executed on Windows with Python 3.13.15.** Both expected findings appeared in the faulty file and both checks were clean on the corrected file. The [execution record and reports](https://github.com/zwadhams/ToolWiki/blob/main/examples/python-checks/evidence.md) retain the environment and tested input hashes. Other hosts have not been run for this recipe. ## Prepare an isolated environment Use Python 3.13 and the pinned Ruff 0.14.3 and mypy 1.18.2 releases. These versions are a reproducible example, not a recommendation to downgrade an existing project. The target Python version is also set to 3.13 in `pyproject.toml`. On Windows, select an interpreter and check it before creating the environment: ```powershell $Python = "python" & $Python --version ``` Expect `Python 3.13.x`. If that command is missing or reports another version, set `$Python` to your Python 3.13 executable, such as `$Python = "C:\path\to\Python313\python.exe"`, and repeat the check. Continue from `examples/python-checks` once the version matches: ```powershell & $Python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt ``` On Linux or macOS, use `.venv/bin/python` in place of the Windows interpreter path. Installing the pinned packages requires package-index access. The fixture has no application dependencies or service credentials. ## Check the faulty version Run both checks and keep their reports: ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe run_checks.py bad --output reports/bad ``` The runner verifies versions, runs each tool separately, and saves commands, input hashes, host details, versions, and return codes in `run.json`. Diagnostics go in `ruff.json` and `mypy.txt`, with separate stderr files. Read both reports. Use a new output directory for each rerun; the runner refuses to overwrite earlier reports. It records setup failures and retains partial output on timeout. The expected signals are: | Tool | Expected finding | Meaning | | ---- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Ruff | `F401` for `math` | The imported module is unused. | | mypy | `arg-type` at `greeting("three")` | The argument is text, but the parameter is annotated as an integer. | The runner returns `1` when the checks complete with findings, `0` when both complete without findings, and `2` when either cannot complete. These are this runner's gate rules, not universal analyzer exit codes. Tool completion is recorded separately from the gate in `run.json`. ## Check the correction The corrected file removes the unused import and calls `greeting(3)`. Run the same configuration against it: ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe run_checks.py good --output reports/good ``` Both reports should be clean for this fixture. The known defects and correction show that the selected checks are active. They do not measure general defect coverage or prove that the program meets every requirement. ## Use it on your project `run_checks.py` accepts only `bad` and `good`; it is a demonstration runner. For your code, run the tools directly. From `examples/python-checks`, keep the checker interpreter's absolute path, then enter your project's root: ```powershell $CheckPython = (Resolve-Path .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe).Path Set-Location "C:\path\to\YOUR_PROJECT" ``` Replace `C:\path\to\YOUR_PROJECT` with your project directory. Use its existing analyzer configuration. If it has none, add these tables to its root `pyproject.toml`, creating the file only if absent. Merge settings into any existing tables instead of replacing the file: ```toml [tool.ruff] target-version = "py313" [tool.ruff.lint] select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"] [tool.mypy] python_version = "3.13" strict = true show_error_codes = true pretty = false ``` Match both target-version settings to the Python version your project supports. The fixture selects only `F401`; this starting selection adds other Pyflakes and selected pycodestyle checks. Review the [Ruff configuration](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/) for your project. If your settings live in `ruff.toml` or `mypy.ini`, use those paths in the corresponding config arguments below. The checker environment needs access to your project's dependencies and type stubs. Install the project's declared dependencies and needed stub packages in that environment, or use a project environment with the checkers installed by setting `$CheckPython` to its interpreter. Resolve [missing imports and stubs](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html#missing-imports) before treating a clean result as useful type coverage. Choose one small source directory and a new report directory for this run: ```powershell $Target = ".\src\YOUR_PACKAGE" $Reports = ".\check-reports\first-run" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Reports -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null & $CheckPython -m ruff check --no-fix --no-cache --config pyproject.toml ` --output-format json $Target > "$Reports\ruff.json" 2> "$Reports\ruff.stderr.txt" $RuffExit = $LASTEXITCODE $RuffExit | Set-Content "$Reports\ruff.exit.txt" & $CheckPython -m mypy --no-incremental --cache-dir "$Reports\mypy-cache" ` --config-file pyproject.toml $Target > "$Reports\mypy.txt" 2> "$Reports\mypy.stderr.txt" $MypyExit = $LASTEXITCODE $MypyExit | Set-Content "$Reports\mypy.exit.txt" ``` Replace `src\YOUR_PACKAGE` with the directory you want checked. Use a different `$Reports` path for every run; stop if directory creation fails. These commands make no automatic source fixes. Read `ruff.json`, `mypy.txt`, and both stderr files with their separate exit codes. Ruff returns `0` for no findings, `1` for findings, and `2` for a failed run. A completed mypy run reports either success or a diagnostic summary; an empty report or a setup error is not a clean result. Review and correct findings, then repeat with a new report directory. Record the source revision, selected configuration, exclusions, and environment using the [run record](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/run-record/). Keep diagnostics separate; do not compare raw issue counts as measures of quality. Use the [CI result-handling guide](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/ci-checks/) to decide which completed findings block a change and how to retain failed or incomplete runs. ## Sources - [Python virtual environments](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/venv.html) - [Ruff rule selection and exit behavior](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/) - [Ruff 0.14.3 distribution](https://pypi.org/project/ruff/0.14.3/) - [mypy 1.18.2 distribution](https://pypi.org/project/mypy/1.18.2/) - [mypy file and import scope](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html) "}
